svg.title: For ⟨E(−h), x⟩, the corresponding coefficients are inLx(h, . . . , h)/ √ n!. Apply (TR22) to th for every positive real t. The identical positive Gaussian factors cancel. The resulting power series is zero for every t > 0, and each coefficient is zero. One can justify coefficient uniqueness without an analytic-series theorem: after the first N coefficients vanish, divide by tN; the tail is dominated for 0 < t ≤1 by the absolutely summable series at t = 1, so t ↓0 recovers the next coefficient.
